dedupe_keys.name: farm twin open source digital twin platform for dairy farming sruc

description: farm-twin is an open-source digital twin platform for dairy farms that builds a virtual representation of the farm system, from individual animals to infrastructure, from real-time sensor, telemetry and other data. It aggregates data from different vendors, such as animal health records, milk production, feed intake and environmental conditions, into one platform with dashboards; supports predictive analytics that combine milk yield trends with health data to flag illness early; and can automate actions, for example triggering a shedding gate to isolate a cow and notifying the farmer. It was developed by the Dairy Research and Innovation Centre of SRUC (Scotland's Rural College) near Dumfries, funded by the Digital Dairy Chain, part of a UKRI Strength in Places programme. Coverage is generic: it was developed in Scotland and is described as suitable for farms of all sizes. The code is free to download, use, modify and distribute, and developers are invited to write adapters for new technologies. Caveats: the announcement read does not name the licence, repository, release date or supported devices, so these must be checked before use. For simulation it gives a live data layer for dairy farm digital twins and supports more precise modelling of herd health and farm conditions, including how heat stress or feed disruption would affect production. It is related to the farmOS record in this catalogue, an open-source farm record system.
